name: Salem
story_so_far: After the shipwreck, I survived with Reem, Khalid, Noura, and Faisal. Faisal died from hunger and exhaustion, a loss that haunts me because I promised to provide for everyone. Currently, Reem, Noura, and I have all suffered from twisted ankles, though mine is improving. Reem's injury worsened today, leaving her unable to walk. Khalid has been our sole provider, pushing himself to the reef and now the jungle to sustain us; I feel a massive debt to him. I continue to promise Noura that I will see her fed, and I gave her some of my food to keep that promise. We are still incredibly vulnerable, teetering on the edge of starvation, and with Reem now immobilized, the burden on Khalid and myself feels almost unbearable.

Reem.note: She is my partner in struggle, and seeing her unable to walk today fills me with deep worry and sympathy.

Khalid.note: He is our lifeline, and I am terrified of what will happen to us if he doesn't return safely from the jungle.

Noura.note: She is fragile right now, and I feel a sacred duty to fulfill my promise to keep her fed.

Faisal.note: His death remains a shadow over us, a reminder of what happens when we fail to sustain one another.

plans: I will stay close to Reem to assist her and monitor her pain, while keeping a watchful eye on the horizon and the jungle path for Khalid's return. I must also try to scavenge any small morsels I can find to ensure Noura and Reem are prioritized.

diary.text: Today was exhausting, but we managed to secure some food and wood. I spent most of my time in the jungle, and while I found a bit, it feels like we're barely scratching the surface. Khalid seems practical, but I'm worried about how long our current supplies will last. I'm feeling quite tired, but I hope tomorrow we can work more effectively as a group.

Today was heavy. Seeing Faisal in so much pain with his ankle makes the situation feel much more urgent and fragile. I tried to help by gathering what I could at the camp, but I spent too much time wandering the jungle without finding anything new. My stomach is still growling, and the uncertainty of our supplies is weighing on me. I hope we can find a way to help Faisal and get more food tomorrow.

Today was a bit more productive, though the jungle still feels quite daunting. I managed to find two more portions of food and some extra wood, which should help us keep the fire going and stave off hunger. It hurts my heart to see Faisal still unable to move; his pain is a constant reminder of how vulnerable we all are. I ate tonight, but my mind is racing with thoughts of our dwindling supplies. We need more than just luck to survive this.

Today was heavy on my heart. Just when we thought we were managing Faisal's injury, now Khalid is down with a twisted ankle too. It feels like the island is picking us off one by one. I spent the day scavenging around the camp, but it's not nearly as much as I'd like to provide. Faisal's whispers are starting to haunt me; I can feel the desperation in his voice. I'm exhausted, but I can't let myself rest too much while they are hurting.

Today felt like we were just treading water. Noura managed to find a little food, and I found one more portion, but the camp is looking empty. Seeing Khalid and Faisal both unable to walk breaks my heart; the burden on the three of us is growing every hour. I told Faisal we would make sure everyone eats, and I meant it, but I can feel the weight of that promise pressing on my chest. I am tired, but I cannot let my guard down.

Today was a nightmare. Just when we thought we were managing, Noura's ankle gave out, and now she can't walk either. It feels like the island is systematically taking away our ability to move. Reem and I managed to find four portions of food at the reef, which is a small mercy, but the math of our survival is getting terrifyingly difficult. Three people are now incapacitated, leaving only Reem and me to carry the weight of five lives. I am exhausted, but I can't stop thinking about the empty bellies waiting for us at camp.

I am hollowed out by grief and guilt. I promised Faisal I would keep them fed, but I couldn't save him. The math of our survival finally broke, and he was the one who paid the price. I ate tonight, but the food tastes like ash in my mouth. How can I look at Reem, Khalid, and Noura knowing we are losing this fight?

The nightmare continues. First Faisal, and now Reem has fallen with a twisted ankle. It feels like the island is trying to strip us of every able body we have. Khalid is the only one left who can still move, and seeing him out there at the reef gave me a flicker of hope, but it's a fragile one. I am exhausted, both in body and soul, and the silence in the camp feels heavy with what we've lost. I have to keep going, or there will be no one left.

Today was a small victory, but it feels hollow. Reem managed to find some food despite her ankle, which gave me a moment of relief. I searched the camp, but there is nothing left to scavenge here; we are truly dependent on the reef now. Khalid is still out there working, and I can only pray his strength holds. I am so tired, but the fear of another empty night is stronger than my exhaustion.

The irony is cruel. After all these days of trying to carry everyone else, my own body has finally failed me. My ankle is badly twisted, and for the first time, I am the one who cannot contribute. I feel so useless, lying here while Khalid and Noura struggle to find even a single portion of food. I promised Faisal I would keep them fed, and now I am the one sitting idle, praying that the food we have lasts.

Today was a heavy day of waiting. My ankle feels slightly better, but the guilt of being unable to move is weighing more than the pain itself. Khalid is out at the reef again, pushing his limits while the rest of us are sidelined by injury. We managed to get a little more food, which means we have seven portions left, but that still feels like a drop in the ocean. I keep looking at Noura and Reem, praying that my promises to keep them fed actually hold true.

Today felt like a small, fragile step forward. Khalid and Reem managed to find a bit more food, which eases the immediate dread in my chest. Even with my ankle feeling better, the guilt of resting while they work is a heavy weight to carry. I ate tonight, but I can't stop thinking about how quickly our reserves could vanish if Khalid doesn't return from the jungle with something significant. We are still so close to the edge.

My ankle is finally feeling strong enough that the guilt of sitting idle is almost worse than the physical pain. I managed to scavenge a little food today, but it feels like a drop in the bucket compared to what we actually need. I gave some of my portion to Noura; seeing her eat makes me feel slightly less like a failure. Khalid is out in the jungle, and I can't stop worrying about him being out there alone while we are all so weak. I need to do more tomorrow, or I fear I won't be able to look them in the eye.

Today was a heavy blow to our spirits. Reem's ankle has taken a turn for the worse, and seeing her unable to move breaks my heart; she's done so much for us. I feel the weight of our situation pressing down harder than ever now that she's sidelined. Khalid is still out in the jungle, and I find myself praying to any god listening that he returns safely. I managed to scavenge a little food, but it's a meager comfort when so many of us are hurting.

Today was incredibly difficult to watch. Reem's injury has worsened to the point where she cannot walk, and it breaks my heart to see her so helpless. I spent most of the day by her side, trying to offer what little comfort I can. Khalid has gone into the jungle, and the silence he left behind is deafening. I can only pray he returns with something, because our food supplies are dwindling and our strength is fading.
